question: Should OpenClaw bundle this 1Password SecretRef resolver, including its trusted-local-`op` execution and service-account-token boundary, and authorize the exact dependency-graph change?
rationale: The generic SecretRef integration pattern exists, but accepting a bundled external CLI that receives a credential and approving a new package dependency are repository security and supply-chain decisions rather than a mechanical contributor repair.

options.title: Approve with evidence
options.body: Authorize the exact dependency change after security review and require an inspectable redacted current-head live transcript or artifact before merge.

options.title: Keep manual exec wiring
options.body: Decline the bundled resolver and retain the existing generic exec-provider route for operators who need 1Password-backed SecretRefs.

options.title: Externalize the integration
options.body: Require the SecretRef provider to ship as an external plugin if maintainers do not want this credential-execution boundary in the bundled distribution.

recommendation.title: Approve with evidence
recommendation.body: Authorize the exact dependency change after security review and require an inspectable redacted current-head live transcript or artifact before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They carried the closest merged SecretRef reference implementation and can provide design context, while the final security and dependency approval remains a repository-owner decision.
